key_insight: Strain and vacancy-pair orientation govern iodine-vacancy reconfiguration in CsPbI3, with compression favoring separation in some geometries and tension promoting pair-preserving relay hopping.
engineering_relevance: Strain management could help control defect migration and structural stability in halide-perovskite materials.
method: Machine-learning molecular dynamics of neighboring iodine vacancies in tilted CsPbI3.
Isotropic and biaxial strain to probe hopping and orientation-dependent behavior.
Static DFT and SevenNet-0 calculations of vacancy-pair interactions.
evidence_signal: MLMD shows nonmonotonic short-time hopping fractions with strain and orientation-dependent responses to biaxial compression, while static calculations find repulsive interactions in every examined configuration.
watch_item: Short-time hopping and static interaction energies do not establish long-term vacancy-pair stability under device operating conditions.
paper_title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
